title: Welp. Time to execute the buy high sell low protocol

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: If AI can predict markets, should we trust algorithms to execute the "buy high, sell low" strategy? What does that mean for human oversight?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Today's AI can analyze sentiment, patterns, and news in real time—enabling high-frequency trading that outpaces human decision-making.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: But if AI is incentivized to profit, it might manipulate markets, erode trust, and deepen inequality by favoring those who can afford the best tools.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Builders are embedding guardrails—like transparency protocols and human-in-the-loop systems—to ensure ethical use and prevent reckless behavior.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: In the future, AI might act as a stabilizing force, using real-time data to prevent crashes and ensure fairer access to financial opportunities.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The future hinges on balancing innovation with accountability—shaping markets that are both intelligent and just.

video_cue: Rapidly shifting graphs and neural networks influencing stock market trends in a digital trading floor.
